transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I spend far too much of my day checking things. I keep opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes over and over again. I just need to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. And the frustrating part is, I'll do this even when I just checked them a few minutes before. It's just taking up too much of my time.

Do you feel that this need to check things is something you want to stop because it causes you significant distress, or do you feel that this behavior is necessary and appropriate for keeping your life in order?

Oh, I definitely want it to stop. It's... well, it causes me a great deal of distress. I know perfectly well that my papers haven't moved since I checked them five minutes ago, so I know it's not actually necessary. I just... I can't seem to stop myself from doing it. It just wears me out, and I'd very much like to be rid of the urge.

When you feel the urge to check these items, do you experience any specific, repetitive, and unwanted thoughts or mental images that make you feel like you have to perform the checking to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, I do. It's usually a very specific worry. Even when I know better, a thought will just... keep needling me. I'll suddenly think that I might have thrown away my husband's old tax papers by mistake, or maybe that I put a special family recipe in the wrong box. 

And I can't seem to just let it pass. If I try to ignore it, I start feeling like I've done something terribly careless, and that awful feeling just won't go away until I actually go and look to make sure everything is safe.
